sources.title: GPT-5 nano model documentation
sources.evidence: Identifies gpt-5-nano and its 2025-08-07 default snapshot. Documents 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input, 128,000 maximum output, text/image inputs, text output, reasoning, function calling, file uploads and prompt caching. Currently marked deprecated. Reopened October 27, 2026 through the official documentation tool and the fresh complete Markdown cache; neither the model details nor comparison table supplies a nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5 for developers
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The August 7, 2025 API announcement identifies gpt-5-nano as one of three sizes and distinguishes these reasoning API models from the ChatGPT router/non-reasoning model. Availability and detailed benchmark tables include the exact nano model, but publish no nominal total or active parameter count.

sources.title: GPT-5 System Card
sources.evidence: Reopened the original 60-page PDF October 27, 2026 and searched its complete freshly extracted text for parameter/count terminology; inspected Introduction, Model Data and Training, nano hallucination comparisons and Appendix 1 Tables 23–26. It names the API variant gpt-5-thinking-nano, describes reinforcement-learning reasoning training and reports safety/image evaluations. No nominal total or active parameter count was found. The Table 1 predecessor relationship to GPT-4.1 nano is not a count or an unchanged-base statement.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide expressly applies to pre-GPT-5.6 models. It explains prompt caching through Transformer attention-layer key/value projections and names gpt-5-nano in its cached-input pricing table. This supports broad Transformer structure when joined to the exact model caching feature, without disclosing a complete architecture.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Documents PDF input processing for vision-capable models: extracted text and page images are provided to the model. Responses accepts input_file; Chat Completions accepts PDF file content parts. This establishes an API file format, not a third native neural modality.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.evidence: June 11, 2026 notice lists gpt-5-nano and gpt-5-nano-2025-08-07 for shutdown on December 11, 2026. Deprecation begins at notice; shutdown is later and was still future at review.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Effective January 1, 2026, governs API services. Sections 2.2 and 9.1 grant limited service access while reserving service intellectual-property rights; supports a proprietary service classification, not an open model-weight license.

sources.title: All models
sources.evidence: Current catalog lists GPT-5 nano as a deprecated API model, separately from its explicit open-weight section, which lists gpt-oss models under Apache 2.0. No nano weight distribution is documented here.

sources.title: GPT-5.1 Instant and GPT-5.1 Thinking System Card Addendum
sources.evidence: Reopened the original November 12, 2025 addendum October 27, 2026 and read its complete freshly extracted text, including Tables 1–3. The comparisons cover GPT-5/5.1 thinking and instant models, not GPT-5 nano, and disclose no nano total or active count. No sibling count is transferred.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4 mini and nano
sources.evidence: Reopened March 17, 2026 announcement October 27, 2026. It calls GPT-5.4 nano an upgrade over GPT-5 nano; its benchmark table compares GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini/nano and GPT-5 mini. It provides no nominal total or active count for original GPT-5 nano and no explicit unchanged-base lineage.

sources.title: Task-Aware Evaluation and Error-Overlap Analysis for Large Language Models
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched the complete original PDF October 27, 2026 and inspected Table 1 and its caption (PDF page 6). The GPT-5 Nano row states Parameters: Undisclosed. The caption distinguishes active counts in parentheses for other models, but supplies none for nano. This is an independent original research comparison, not an OpenAI disclosure; its unsupported MoE label is not adopted.

sources.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on the 2026 Korean CSAT Mathematics Exam
sources.publisher: Goun Pyeon et al. / Chungnam National University
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched the complete original author-hosted PDF October 27, 2026 and inspected Section 4.1 and Table 2 (PDF page 12). The exact GPT-5-nano row gives an active-parameter scale of approximately 15B with an asterisk. The caption explicitly identifies starred values as estimates from prior documentation and reported performance. This performance-based estimate is excluded from the parameter specification.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Reopened original v2 HTML October 27, 2026 and inspected abstract, effective-capacity methodology and exact gpt-5-nano/gpt-5-nano-think rows; also checked the freshly extracted PDF text. Reported size bands are calibrated open-model-equivalent knowledge capacity from black-box probes, not disclosed production total or active counts, and are excluded.

sources.title: Nemotron 3 Nano: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
sources.evidence: Reopened the original later model-team report October 27, 2026 and checked its parameter/benchmark comparisons plus full HTML search for GPT-5. Its explicit total and active disclosures concern Nemotron 3 Nano and its open-model comparisons; no GPT-5 nano entry or count was found. NVIDIA Nano and OpenAI nano are distinct models.

name.note: Official documentation uses GPT-5 nano in the title and GPT-5 Nano in its body; existing display capitalization is retained.

developer.note: Original first-party developer announcement and exact API documentation identify OpenAI.

family.note: The API nano belongs to GPT-5. The generic baseline gpt-nano grouping merges distinct generations.

release_date.note: Original dated announcement explicitly says nano is available now in the API; this establishes release day independently of its snapshot suffix.

open_weights.note: Documented as hosted API access under retained service rights, separate from the publisher's open-weight models; no nano weights are offered in these sources.

license.note: Descriptive classification of the hosted service terms; not a named downloadable-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no published nominal total for the exact GPT-5 nano variant in official specifications, launch benchmarks, original GPT-5 card or later comparisons. Complete cached official model text and both original cards were searched, with relevant sections/tables inspected. CHOMPS Table 1 labels nano undisclosed; IKP black-box capacity bands are not model specifications. No documented counted-base lineage supports a nominal inference.

active_parameters_b.note: Separately searched for active/activated-parameter disclosures, including later original research comparisons. No supported nominal active count was found for exact GPT-5 nano. CHOMPS Table 1 leaves its count undisclosed; CNU CSAT Table 2 explicitly estimates its approximately 15B active scale from documentation/performance, so that value is excluded. IKP measures black-box effective capacity; NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano has no GPT-5 comparison row. No dense equality or sibling transfer is assumed.

architecture.note: Cross-source inference: exact nano documentation enables prompt_caching, and OpenAI's applicable pre-GPT-5.6 technical guide both names nano and describes Transformer-layer KV attention. This supports broad Transformer structure only, not an exclusively Transformer block inventory, layer/head counts, dense versus MoE routing, or parameter count. Exact-name training/interpretability searches and later reports did not establish those details.

context_window.note: Documented total context window; separate maximum input/output budgets are 272,000/128,000 tokens, not substitutes for context.

modalities.note: Native inputs are text/image and output is text. PDF is included under the catalog's API-format convention: exact nano supports vision/file uploads, and the file guide specifies PDF extraction to text/page images. Calling the image-generation tool does not make images native model output.

reasoning.note: Exact model supports reasoning tokens. The system card names this API variant gpt-5-thinking-nano and describes its reasoning training, separately from non-reasoning chat models.

tool_call.note: Exact documentation lists function calling and Responses tools; original launch explicitly includes nano in custom and parallel tool support.

description.value: GPT-5 nano is an API reasoning model with text and image inputs, text output, and function calling.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported routing/bulk-job slogan with documented capabilities of this exact variant.

patch.notes: The original API nano is gpt-5-thinking-nano in the GPT-5 system card, not the ChatGPT router or a GPT-5.4 nano variant. Published nominal total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the checked sources; performance-based size estimates are excluded. The broad transformer label is a cross-source inference from exact nano prompt-caching support and OpenAI's pre-GPT-5.6 KV-attention explanation, which also names nano; it does not establish the complete block design, dense/MoE routing or counts. PDF denotes API extraction to text and page images; native input modalities are text and image, with text output. The 400,000 context window has separate 272,000 maximum-input and 128,000 maximum-output limits. As of 2026-10-27 the model is deprecated, with shutdown scheduled for 2026-12-11; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retained explicit null total and active counts after reopening exact official documentation, the original GPT-5 system card, later GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.4 comparisons, and original research tables. No published nominal count or counted-base lineage was found. CHOMPS marks nano undisclosed; CNU CSAT and IKP size estimates do not establish production counts. All twelve other field assessments and prior corrections are preserved.
